kicker: Dairy · EBITDA margin, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
title: Costlier milk squeezed pouches, not paneer
dek: Heritage and Dodla paid 11–16% more for milk in Q2 FY27 but raised milk prices only 6–8%; their margins fell 1.3–3.7 pt. Milky Mist and Parag, which sell paneer, cheese, yogurt and whey, widened theirs.

read: Paneer, cheese and whey can be repriced faster than pouch milk; Q3 tests whether Dodla's and Heritage's late hikes catch up while Parag sees milk holding near ₹46.5 a litre.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls of Milky Mist, Parag, Heritage and Dodla
notes: EBITDA margins are from filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated; Hatsun standalone). Milky Mist listed recently, so its year-ago margin is the company-reported 14.0% from its Q2 call, against a reported 15.2% now; excluding other income its Q2 FY27 margin was about 14.5%. Parag's call puts its margin at 8.1% vs 7.3% after excluding a one-off forex gain in the base; reported profit fell 8%. Milk cost and selling-price changes are year-on-year as stated on the Q2 calls (Heritage: procurement +11% to ₹47.73/L, milk price +6%; Dodla: ₹43.2/L vs ₹37.3, realisation ₹61.9/L vs ₹57.3). Hatsun held no Q2 call on the desk and is grouped as milk-led on its own disclosures. Dodla guides to a 7.5–8% margin in H2 as its September price rise flows through.
